The Federal Government is set to integrate key export regulatory agencies into the National Single Window platform on December 14 as part of efforts to simplify trade procedures, reduce bureaucratic bottlenecks and improve the efficiency of Nigeria’s import and export processes. The Project Coordinator of the National Single Window, Tola Fakolade, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ engagement on the platform in Abuja on Tuesday, saying the first batch of agencies would comprise regulators responsible for processing export-related documentation. He said the second batch, scheduled to incorporate additional agencies and processes, would include the Central Bank of Nigeria, the Nigeria Export Proceeds system and operators in the free trade zones. Fakolade said the project team was working with commercial banks to ensure their integration into the platform, adding that the implementation had been divided into two batches to ensure a smooth transition. “We have reached a milestone on the National Single Window. We are working with the commercial banks to onboard them on the National Single Window. What we have done is to categorise them into two batches. “The regulatory part of it is what we are putting in batch one, and all the NXPs and mostly the CBN processes, together with the free trade zones, for those who operate at the Free Zone, will be in the second batch,” he said. He expressed confidence that the first batch would go live as scheduled, although he admitted that the project team was under pressure to complete outstanding activities ahead of the launch. “I am happy to say that the first batch is going live on the 14th of December, 2026. Even though myself and my team look like we are smiling, I can assure you it is burning inside because there is still a whole lot of work to do, but we will get there,” Fakolade stated. According to him, the testing involves giving selected exporters access to a controlled environment where they can use the platform and provide feedback on its functionality. “We take a sample of exporters, and we actually tell them to feel the system, let them work with the system, of course in a very closed environment, to provide feedback on the system. We also do the same with our agency partners, to say, come and look at what we have been doing and give us feedback on how we can improve the system,” he said. Fakolade added that nationwide training for stakeholders began on November 16, with physical training centres established in Lagos and Port Harcourt. He urged exporters, agents and other users to register for the two-day practical training, saying participants would be provided with laptops to gain hands-on experience with the platform. “It is really, really important. It is a two-day training, and it will really, really help you, so that when we launch, you already have some familiarity with the system. We want you to have a great user experience when we launch on the 14th of December,” he said. The project coordinator explained that the first batch would automate export-related regulatory processes involving agencies such as the Standards Organisation of Nigeria, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, the Nigerian Export Promotion Council and the Nigeria Agricultural Quarantine Service. He said further engagement would take place ahead of the second batch, particularly with the CBN and other institutions responsible for processing export proceeds and related transactions. The December deployment comes as the Federal Government seeks to build on the gains recorded in the first phase of the initiative, which was inaugurated by President Bola Tinubu on April 16, 2024, and went live on March 27, 2026. The National Single Window is designed as a centralised electronic platform connecting government agencies and private-sector operators involved in international trade. It seeks to eliminate repetitive documentation, harmonise regulatory requirements, improve transparency and reduce the time and cost of clearing goods across Nigeria’s borders. At a press briefing last month, Fakolade said the platform had registered 12,112 importers and agents, while more than 8,000 users had received training. He also reported a system uptime of 99.98 per cent. The first phase automated the submission, processing and approval of licences, permits and certificates issued by NAFDAC, SON, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency and NAQS. It also covered payments for relevant permits and certificates, as well as air and sea cargo manifests, excluding oil and gas-related operations. Fakolade said the platform had processed 156,026 licences and permits, comprising 104,956 documents for SON, 50,622 for NAFDAC and 398 for NAQS. He added that the number of licences and permits issued by SON and NAFDAC had increased by between 20 and 30 per cent compared with the corresponding period before the platform was introduced. The next phase is expected to extend the integration to more institutions and trade-related financial processes, bringing Nigeria closer to a unified electronic system for international trade.
